governance.note: Byte-faithful re-solve of the run150 keeper recipe (run143 lineage + per-year RTORDPA overlay + ERCOT zonal gas basis EP anchor + the PRB gas-ref fix + the ST_GAS net-load reliability-drag min-gen floor) plus ONE new lever this session: the coal PRB passthrough-sigmoid CHEAP-GAS FLOOR restored to its documented breakeven. The keeper had carried a fitted-DOWN PRB floor (baseload 0.73, load-follower tier 0.63) below the documented COAL_SIGMOID_DEFAULTS[(ERCOT,prb)] breakeven of 0.78. Those deeper floors were silently compensating for the pre-drag ST_GAS under-run; once the run150 ST_GAS net-load drag floor pulled gas share back onto ST_GAS, the over-discounted PRB coal over-ran out of merit (+10.6 / +13.2 / +2.2 % in 2023/24/25) and stole the energy that should sit on CC_REGULAR/ST_GAS (CC_REGULAR was left -3.5 / -4.8 / -0.0 %). This session sets BOTH PRB tiers (baseload and load-follower) to the single documented breakeven floor 0.78 (coal_prb_passthrough_floor=0.78, coal_prb_follower_floor=0.78). Physical, not dialed to TWh: 0.78 IS the curated per-month PRB-vs-gas-CC delivered-cost breakeven (run-70s tuning series), and the cheap-gas fuel passthrough of railed PRB is a basin/contract (take-or-pay) property, not a duty-cycle property, so baseload and cycling PRB share the same cheap-gas floor; the follower tier KEEPS its distinct dear-gas ceiling (1.35 vs baseload 1.50), so the cyclers still mark up less than baseload at high gas. The lever is gas-keyed, so it self-targets the cheap-gas year (2024, $2.2 gas) where the over-run is worst and barely moves the dear-gas years. Result: COAL_PRB lands +2.7 / -1.3 / +0.1 % (over-run CLOSED, C2 coal family now PASSES) and the freed MWh conserves to CC_REGULAR (-1.7 / -1.3 / +0.5 %) plus a little ST_GAS, with NO spill onto CT_PEAKER (the pre-existing zonal-gas relocation over-run moves <+0.2 TWh) and NO leakage to slack (system volume conserved). LMP unchanged vs the run150 baseline (MAE 27.9 / 15.3 / 11.4 vs 27.8 / 15.2 / 11.4; duration curves byte-comparable) — the lever rebalances within-thermal volume, not price. No adder/haircut/sigmoid tuned to a price or volume residual; no unit pinned to CEMS; no input rescaled to land on actuals. All active levers trace to measured/physical inputs: CAMPD net-load-filtered outage windows, measured 2023 storage-AS + load-RRS-UFR credits, EIA-860 BTM CHP host steam out of the LP, per-plant F923 delivered fuel, measured EP-anchored zonal gas basis, CAMPD-fitted ST_GAS net-load drag curve, documented PRB-vs-gas-CC breakeven passthrough, published NP6-576-ER ORDC params, measured RTORDPA overlay. Doc: docs/ercot-coal-prb-passthrough-floor-2026-06.md.
governance.coal_prb_resolved: The COAL_PRB / coal-family over-run that prior keepers (run145..run150) carried as an ACCEPTED out-of-scope sysvol caveat is RESOLVED by this lever: C2 coal now PASSES (coal family +1.4% in 2024 vs +12.4% at the run150 baseline), so it is no longer in the exceptions ledger.
governance.stgas_drag_rationale: ST_GAS C1 now PASSES in all three years (was the chronic under-run -31.6 / -56.8 / -49.1 % before the run150 ST_GAS net-load reliability-drag min-gen floor; doc docs/ercot-st-gas-netload-drag-2026-06.md). The drag floor is a CAMPD-fitted, net-load-indexed reliability-dispatch trigger (a physical availability/reliability event, forward-defensible), not a fit to ST_GAS volume.
